title: select().fetch() behaves differently in core and ORM
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/8090
Originally posted by **kdwyer** June 3, 2022 On Postgresql, `select().fetch()` behaves correctly in core, but not in the ORM. Versions: - PostgreSQL 13.7 on x86_64-suse-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (SUSE Linux) 7.5.0, 64-bit - psycopg2-binary 2.9.3 - SQLAlchemy 1.4.37 Given this initial setup: ```python import sqlalchemy as sa from sqlalchemy import orm Base = orm.declarative_base() class Model(Base): __tablename__ = 'tbl' id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True) dbname = 'test' FUTURE = True engine = sa.create_engine(f'postgresql+psycopg2:///{dbname}', echo=True, future=FUTURE) Base.metadata.drop_all(engine) Base.metadata.create_all(engine) Session = orm.sessionmaker(engine, future=FUTURE) with Session.begin() as s: s.add_all([Model() for _ in range(6)]) ``` This core code ```python with engine.connect() as conn: models = Model.__table__ q = sa.select(models).order_by(models.c.id).fetch(2) for model in conn.execute(q): print(model.id) q = sa.select(models).order_by(models.c.id).offset(3).fetch(2) for model in conn.execute(q): print(model.id) ``` generates the output that I would expect: ```none 2022-06-03 08:15:28,847 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine SELECT tbl.id FROM tbl ORDER BY tbl.id FETCH FIRST (%(param_1)s) ROWS ONLY 2022-06-03 08:15:28,847 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00064s] {'param_1': 2} 1 2 2022-06-03 08:15:28,850 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine SELECT tbl.id FROM tbl ORDER BY tbl.id OFFSET (%(param_1)s) ROWS FETCH FIRST (%(param_2)s) ROWS ONLY 2022-06-03 08:15:28,850 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00034s] {'param_1': 3, 'param_2': 2} 4 5 ``` However this ORM code ```python with Session() as s: q = sa.select(Model).order_by(Model.id).fetch(2) for model in s.scalars(q): print(model.id) q = sa.select(Model).order_by(Model.id).offset(3).fetch(2) for model in s.scalars(q): print(model.id) ``` omits the `FETCH` when no `OFFSET` is present, returning all rows, and emits `LIMIT ALL` when `OFFSET` is present. ```none 2022-06-03 08:15:28,852 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine SELECT tbl.id FROM tbl ORDER BY tbl.id 2022-06-03 08:15:28,852 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00019s] {} 1 2 3 4 5 6 2022-06-03 08:15:28,854 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine SELECT tbl.id FROM tbl ORDER BY tbl.id LIMIT ALL OFFSET %(param_1)s 2022-06-03 08:15:28,854 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine [generated in 0.00019s] {'param_1': 3} 4 5 6 ``` I didn't find anything in the docs to explain why `select().fetch()` would behave differently in the ORM in the docs. Am I missing something?
